why: upstream constructs from a node handle, a topic, a QoS and an allocator, all as `shared_ptr`-shaped arguments. Ours is DEFAULT-constructed and filled by `rclcpp::Node::create_publisher(pub.publisher(), topic)` -- the same out-reference creation every entity in this API uses (RFC-0022: no allocator, so a constructor cannot fail and cannot hand back a handle). See `cpp:LifecycleNode::add_managed_entity` for why the node does not do it for you. FILED HERE, not in `lifecycle/`, because the topic classifier keys on the NAME: this is a lifecycle row and the shard is the taxonomy's answer, not a claim about the subject (same observation as `cpp:LifecycleNode::get_transition_graph`).
